Other links refer to a link by touching its middle. A reference\n// to 0 (nothing) is a free end, a reference to the link itself is a loop that\n// returns to its own middle, so (1: 1 1) is a symmetric figure eight (∞).\n//\n// Geometry is computed in layout units (neighbouring middles are 1 apart),\n// every curve is a chain of cubic Bézier segments that share tangents where\n// they meet, and the finished drawing is scaled into a SIZE × SIZE box.\n\nexport const SIZE = 100;\nexport const STROKE = 2.4;\n/** One colour per real link: link 1, 2, 3, 4. */\nexport const COLORS = ['#22d3ee', '#c084fc', '#f472b6', '#facc15'];\n\nconst PAD = 9; [**Problem Formulation**](https://github.com/Konard/problem-solving/blob/main/problem-solving/problem-formulation/problem-formulation.md): This step involves fully understanding and defining the problem that needs to be solved. This includes defining the problem in clear, precise terms and breaking it down into smaller, manageable parts. Alongside this understanding, you also formulate failing tests based on the problem's definition. These tests serve as concrete goals that the solution should achieve. The aim of this step is to transform the initial problem into a well-defined set of failing tests that clearly express what a solution to the problem should look like.\n\n2. [**Solution Implementation**](https://github.com/Konard/problem-solving/blob/main/problem-solving/solution-implementation/solution-implementation.md): This step begins with formulating a plan to pass the tests defined in the previous step. With a clear understanding of what the solution should achieve (as defined by the tests), you write just enough code to pass these tests. This promotes a focus on solving the problem at hand without overcomplicating the solution. After making the tests pass, you refine the solution through debugging and refactoring to improve its structure and performance without changing its behavior. This step is iterative and may involve revisiting the problem formulation stage if new information or difficulties arise, or if the tests need to be updated. Finally, documenting the solution for future reference and for others' understanding is an integral part of this step.\n\nNote: On any step of the algorithm it is possible that problem definition will change or is required to be changed for  solution to be possible or efficient. In that case we should start again with decomposion (the first Almost anything that can be done with files in a repository can be automated.\n\n| Feature                      | What It Means For You                                                                                                                                                      |\n| ---------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **No Babysitting**           | Full autonomous mode with sudo access. AI has creative freedom like a real programmer.                                                                                     |\n| **Cloud Isolation**          | Runs on dedicated VMs or Docker. Easy to restore if broken.                                                                                                                |\n| **Full Internet + Sudo**     | AI can install packages, fetch docs, and configure the system as needed.                                                                                                   |\n| **Pre-installed Toolchain**  | 25GB+ ready: 10 language runtimes, 2 theorem provers, build tools. Can install more.                                                                                       |\n| **Token Efficiency**         | Routine tasks automated in code, so AI tokens focus on creative problem-solving.                                                                                           |\n| **Time Freedom**             | What takes humans 2-8 hours, AI completes each working session in 10-25 minutes. Mass execution of tasks in repository is possible. \"The code is written while you sleep.\" |\n| **Scale with Orchestration** | Parallel workers feel like a team of developers. Pair Claude MAX and ChatGPT Pro ($200 each) for two independent unlimited budgets.                                        |\n| **Human Control**            | AI creates draft PRs - you decide what merges. Quality gates where they matter.                                                                                            |\n| **Any Device Programming**   | Manage AI from any device with `/solve` and `/hive` via Telegram bot. No PC, IDE, or laptop required.                                                                      |\n| **100% Open Source**         | Unlicense (public domain). Full transparency, no vendor lock-in.                                                                                                           |\n\n**Cost**: Hive Mind supports two $200/month subscriptions as full-featured \"unlimited\" options:\n\n| Subscription                                                       | Pairs with `--tool` | Default model | Best for                                                |\n| ------------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------- | ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |\n| **Anthropic Claude MAX** (~$200/month, often 50% off = $400 value) | `claude` (default)  | Opus          | Highest creativity, strongest general code reasoning    |\n| **OpenAI ChatGPT Pro** ($200/month, includes Codex)                | `codex`             | `gpt-6-sol`   | Strong deterministic refactors and fast iteration loops |\n\nBoth tools can be combined in the same hive. Workers can run different tools in parallel, and `/codex` or `/solve --tool codex` routes tasks to ChatGPT Pro while the default routes to Claude MAX. There is no requirement to pick one: either single subscription is enough to operate, and using both unlocks per-tool/model concurrency mode (#1474).\n\nHive Mind has high creativity indistinguishable from average programmers. It asks questions if requirements are unclear, and you can clarify on the go via PR comments.\n\nFor the project's vision and example user journeys, see [docs/VISION.md](./docs/VISION.md). ; attempt++) {\n    try {\n      return execFileSync('gh', argv, { encoding: 'utf8', maxBuffer: 1 << 28, stdio: ['ignore', 'pipe', 'pipe'] });\n    } catch (error) {\n      if (/Not Found|404/.test(String(error.stderr))) return null;\n      if (attempt >= 4) throw error;\n      execFileSync('sleep', [String(attempt * 5)]);\n    }\n  }\n}\n\nconst gql = (query) => JSON.parse(gh(['api', 'graphql', '-f', `query=${query}`]) || '{}').data || {};\nconst quote = (s) => JSON.stringify(s);\nconst BATCH = 20;\n\n// Pass 1: size, files, number of commits and the head commit of every repository.\nconst facts = {};\nfor (let i = 0; i < repos.length; i += BATCH) {\n  const batch = repos.slice(i, i + BATCH);\n  const body = batch\n    .map(\n      (r, k) => `r${k}: repository(owner: ${quote(r.owner)}, name: ${quote(r.name)}) {\n        diskUsage isEmpty\n        object(expression: \"HEAD:\") { ... on Tree { entries { name } } }\n        defaultBranchRef { target { ... on Commit { oid history(first: 1) { totalCount } } } }\n      }`,\n    )\n    .join('\\n');\n  const data = gql(`query { ${body} }`);\n  batch.forEach((r, k) => {\n    const d = data[`r${k}`];\n    if (!d) return log(`missing ${r.fullName}`);\n    const head = d.defaultBranchRef && d.defaultBranchRef.target;\n    facts[r.fullName] = {\n      diskUsage: d.diskUsage,\n      isEmpty: d.isEmpty,\n      files: d.object ? d.object.entries.map((e) => e.name).sort() : [],\n      commits: head ? head.history.totalCount : 0,\n      head: head ? head.oid : null,\n    };\n  });\n  console.error(`pass 1: ${Math.min(i + BATCH, repos.length)}/${repos.length}`);\n}\n\n// Pass 2: the root commit, reached with the \"<head oid> <count - 2>\" history cursor.\nconst withHistory = repos.filter((r) => facts[r.fullName] && facts[r.fullName].head);\nfor (let i = 0; Copies named <client>-<name> without\n// a known original are checked as <client>/<name> as well.\nconst clientPrefix = new RegExp(`^(${CLIENTS.join('|')})-(.+)$`, 'i');\nfor (const r of repos) {\n  const match = r.owner === 'konard' && clientPrefix.exec(r.name);\n  const original = r.copyOf || (match ? `${match[1]}/${match[2]}` : null);\n  if (!original || !facts[r.fullName]) continue;\n  const visibility = gh(['api', `repos/${original}`, '--jq', '.visibility']);\n  facts[r.fullName].upstream = { fullName: original, public: (visibility || '').trim() === 'public' };\n  log(r.fullName, '<-', original, visibility ? visibility.trim() : 'missing');\n}\n\nfs.mkdirSync(path.dirname(OUT), { recursive: true });\nfs.writeFileSync(OUT, JSON.stringify({ collectedAt: new Date().toISOString(), repositories: facts }, null, 1) + '\\n');\nconsole.error(`wrote ${Object.keys(facts).length} repositories to ${path.relative(root, OUT)}`);\n"

With `spacing`, which is the default, the letter shapes stay the same and only the gaps between characters change. With `spacingAndGlyphs`, the glyphs themselves are also stretched (spacing adjusts the spacing between glyphs but does not stretch or squeeze them, while spacingAndGlyphs adjusts both spacing and glyph size.).\n- **Role of `textLength`:** It sets the width the text should occupy. The user agent will ensure that the text does not extend farther than that distance, using the method or methods specified by the lengthAdjust attribute. Microsoft's docs note that this keeps the width stable regardless of conditions including web fonts failing to load (or not having loaded yet).\n- **Elements and DOM:** The attribute applies to `<text>` and `<tspan>` elements. In the DOM, both attributes are exposed as read-only properties on `SVGTextContentElement` (textLength and lengthAdjust reflecting the attributes of the given element).\n- **Compatibility and animation:** The MDN Russian page lists the attribute as well established and works across many devices and browser versions. Root causes\n\n**Rain off the grid.** The old rain used 34 px columns while the CSS background grid has 64 px cells, and the grid\ndrifted on its own CSS animation (`grid-drift`, 24 s) independently of the canvas. Symbols and grid lines could never\nline up and slid apart over time. Now a column is 32 px (half a cell), columns start at x = 0 of the grid, and the\ndrift of the grid is set by the same animation loop that moves the canvas.\n\n**Hidden `S` and the overlapping arrow.** Words were placed at hand-picked offsets with an estimated width. Measuring\nthe old drawing ([`data/psd-old-overlaps.txt`](data/psd-old-overlaps.txt)) shows that \"Solution\" spanned x = 825.6–960\nwhile the final node spans 819–841, so the `S` was painted behind the node, and \"decomposition\" ended at x = 281.9\nwhile its arrow started at x = 280. The fix removes the guesswork: every label has a fixed `textLength`, so its width\ndoes not depend on the font that loaded, and nodes and arrows are computed from those widths. A test checks that no\nlabel touches another label, node or arrow.\n\n**Broken and one-sided links.** The symbols of issue #7 drew a link as separate pieces: a dot for the middle and two\nline segments to the ends. That made every link look split in the middle (img5–img7). A self-reference was a single\nloop on one side (\"eyeglasses\"). Links also all had the same colour. Now each link is one path: bar → own middle →\narrow, built from cubic Bézier segments whose tangents match where they meet. Each link has its own colour. A\nself-reference is a loop mirrored around the middle, so (1: 1 1) is ∞.\n\n**Missing networks.** The old set came from a generator that had no zero link and listed only a sample of networks.\nWith the zero link, N real links have 2N references, each one of N + 1 values. That gives (N + 1)^(2N) networks:\n4, 81, 4,096 and 390,625. Grouping networks that differ only by renaming links 1…N (0 stays fixed) leaves 4, 45, 720\nand 16,900 classes by Burnside's lemma. Brute force in [`data/count-networks.txt`](data/count-networks.txt) gives the\nsame numbers. The gallery shows every network page by page, because 390,625 symbols cannot be drawn at once.\n\n**Organizations, empty repositories and broken forks on the site.** The collection of issue #7 took every non-fork\npublic repository of the user and of every organization they had committed to. It had no notion of value for a\nvisitor. GitHub's `isFork` is false for a repository whose history was pushed rather than forked. That is what\nhappened with konard/slava: 49 of the 54 commits of konard/sbt, for example, are by another person. So such\nrepositories counted as original work. The fix collects health facts for every repository (size, files, root commit,\nupstream visibility) and hides them by explicit rules:\n\n| Reason | Repositories |\n| --- | --- |\n| hidden organization | 32 |\n| empty | 63 |\n| broken fork | 26 |\n| copy of a project that is not public | 86 |\n| deleted since the collection | 1 |\n\nThe full list, with names except for the non-public copies, is in\n[`data/repository-health-rules.txt`](data/repository-health-rules.txt). Only 3 copies of public projects remain,\nshown as forks. Their originals are MixaByk1996's elements-app, laravel-docker-project and gamestock.shop.\n\n**\"Client copies\" wording.** Repositories copied from other people were labelled \"copies of client projects kept for\nhistory\" and counted (89) on the Repositories page. That presented private work as a feature. Now only forks of\npublic projects are shown, and nothing about non-public originals is stored. The collector records just\n`{ \"public\": false }`, with no name.\n\n**Experience \"All\" showed few repositories.** Without a role, the page showed 6 examples per profession\n(`slice(0, 6)`). Now it shows every picked repository of every profession (13 professions, 114 repositories).\n\nThe site before and after:\n\n| | Before | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Original repositories | 525 in 15 organizations | 434 (146 personal, 288 in 8 organizations) |\n| Copies | 89 \"client copies\" | 3 forks of public projects |\n| Mirrors | 96 | 88 |\n| Stars | 993 | 982 |\n| Languages | 73 | 66 |\n| npm packages | 222 | 220 (Homebrew card gone: its only tap was in a hidden organization) |\n\n## 6. External issues\n\nThe issue asks to report problems to other repositories when they are the cause. The candidate was\n[konard/links-visuals](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals), the blueprint the issue refers to. Its `grid.html` and\n`blueprint.html` already draw every link as a single SVG path with its own colour (`getLinkColor`). The defects of\nimg5–img7 came from this site's own renderer (`src/links/glyph.js` of issue #7), not from links-visuals code. They are\nfixed here. links-visuals is an interactive editor and does not enumerate or encode networks, so the zero-link encoding\ndoes not apply to it. No other external project is involved, so no issue was filed.\n\n## 7. Debug tools\n\n| Tool | What it prints |\n| --- | --- |\n| `node experiments/collect-repository-health.cjs [out] --verbose` | Every repository with its root commit author and date, upstream visibility (`<- (not public)` without a name), retries and split batches when GitHub answers 502. |\n| `node experiments/repository-health-rules.cjs` | Every hidden repository grouped by reason; copies of non-public projects only as a count. |\n| `npm run build:data` | Totals and `not shown: 63 empty, 32 hidden organization, 26 broken fork, 86 original is not public, 1 deleted`. |\n| `node experiments/psd-old-overlaps.mjs` | Measured spans of the old diagram labels against nodes and arrows. |\n| `node experiments/count-networks.mjs` | Networks and classes of 1–4 links by brute force and by formula, with the first codes. |\n| `node experiments/contact-sheet.mjs` | A PNG sheet of all symbols of a size, to look at every network at once. |\n\n## 8. Online research and existing components\n\n| Source | Used for |\n| --- | --- |\n| [konard/links-visuals](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals) | The look of a link: a bar at the source, the middle, an arrow at the target, one colour per link, curves with continuous tangents (\"The Continuity of Splines\" by Freya Holmér, credited in its README). |\n| [konard/twittermatrix](https://github.com/konard/twittermatrix) | The digital rain mechanics: one symbol per column per step and a fading trail. |\n| [Burnside's lemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside%27s_lemma) | Counting networks up to renaming links (the \"one per class\" view of the gallery). |\n| [Cubic Bézier curves](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Tutorial/Paths) | Smooth links drawn as SVG paths and as `Path2D` in the rain canvas. |\n| [SVG `textLength` / `lengthAdjust`](https://docs.w3cub.com/svg/reference/attribute/textlength) | Fixed label widths that do not depend on which font is loaded. |\n| [konard/problem-solving](https://github.com/konard/problem-solving) | The original idea and drawing of the universal problem solving algorithm. |\n| [link-assistant/hive-mind](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind), [link-assistant/formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai) | Implementations of the algorithm that the method notes link to. |\n| Musk's five-step engineering process, first step \"make your requirements less dumb\" ([CleanTechnica](https://cleantechnica.com/2021/08/16/elon-musk-reveals-his-5-step-engineering-protocol/), from the 2021 Everyday Astronaut Starbase interview) | The step that sends the solver back to the formulation of the task. |\n\nNo library was added. Drawing 390,625 different networks needs a geometry that is specific to doublet links. Generic\ngraph layout libraries (Cytoscape, d3-force, GoJS, considered in the links-visuals history) draw edges between nodes.\nThey cannot draw links that point to the middles of other links, and they cannot draw self-references that pass\nthrough their own middle.\n\n## 9. Root causes\n\n**Rain off the grid.** The old rain used 34 px columns while the CSS background grid has 64 px cells, and the grid\ndrifted on its own CSS animation (`grid-drift`, 24 s) independently of the canvas. Symbols and grid lines could never\nline up and slid apart over time. Now a column is 32 px (half a cell), columns start at x = 0 of the grid, and the\ndrift of the grid is set by the same animation loop that moves the canvas.\n\n**Hidden `S` and the overlapping arrow.** Words were placed at hand-picked offsets with an estimated width. Measuring\nthe old drawing ([`data/psd-old-overlaps.txt`](data/psd-old-overlaps.txt)) shows that \"Solution\" spanned x = 825.6–960\nwhile the final node spans 819–841, so the `S` was painted behind the node, and \"decomposition\" ended at x = 281.9\nwhile its arrow started at x = 280. The fix removes the guesswork: every label has a fixed `textLength`, so its width\ndoes not depend on the font that loaded, and nodes and arrows are computed from those widths. A test checks that no\nlabel touches another label, node or arrow.\n\n**Broken and one-sided links.** The symbols of issue #7 drew a link as separate pieces: a dot for the middle and two\nline segments to the ends. That made every link look split in the middle (img5–img7). A self-reference was a single\nloop on one side (\"eyeglasses\"). Links also all had the same colour. Now each link is one path: bar → own middle →\narrow, built from cubic Bézier segments whose tangents match where they meet. Each link has its own colour. A\nself-reference is a loop mirrored around the middle, so (1: 1 1) is ∞.\n\n**Missing networks.** The old set came from a generator that had no zero link and listed only a sample of networks.\nWith the zero link, N real links have 2N references, each one of N + 1 values. That gives (N + 1)^(2N) networks:\n4, 81, 4,096 and 390,625. Grouping networks that differ only by renaming links 1…N (0 stays fixed) leaves 4, 45, 720\nand 16,900 classes by Burnside's lemma. Brute force in [`data/count-networks.txt`](data/count-networks.txt) gives the\nsame numbers. The gallery shows every network page by page, because 390,625 symbols cannot be drawn at once.\n\n**Organizations, empty repositories and broken forks on the site.** The collection of issue #7 took every non-fork\npublic repository of the user and of every organization they had committed to. It had no notion of value for a\nvisitor. GitHub's `isFork` is false for a repository whose history was pushed rather than forked. That is what\nhappened with konard/slava: 49 of the 54 commits of konard/sbt, for example, are by another person. So such\nrepositories counted as original work. The fix collects health facts for every repository (size, files, root commit,\nupstream visibility) and hides them by explicit rules:\n\n| Reason | Repositories |\n| --- | --- |\n| hidden organization | 32 |\n| empty | 63 |\n| broken fork | 26 |\n| copy of a project that is not public | 86 |\n| deleted since the collection | 1 |\n\nThe full list, with names except for the non-public copies, is in\n[`data/repository-health-rules.txt`](data/repository-health-rules.txt). Only 3 copies of public projects remain,\nshown as forks. Their originals are MixaByk1996's elements-app, laravel-docker-project and gamestock.shop.\n\n**\"Client copies\" wording.** Repositories copied from other people were labelled \"copies of client projects kept for\nhistory\" and counted (89) on the Repositories page. That presented private work as a feature. Now only forks of\npublic projects are shown, and nothing about non-public originals is stored. The collector records just\n`{ \"public\": false }`, with no name.\n\n**Experience \"All\" showed few repositories.** Without a role, the page showed 6 examples per profession\n(`slice(0, 6)`). Now it shows every picked repository of every profession (13 professions, 114 repositories).\n\nThe site before and after:\n\n| | Before | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Original repositories | 525 in 15 organizations | 434 (146 personal, 288 in 8 organizations) |\n| Copies | 89 \"client copies\" | 3 forks of public projects |\n| Mirrors | 96 | 88 |\n| Stars | 993 | 982 |\n| Languages | 73 | 66 |\n| npm packages | 222 | 220 (Homebrew card gone: its only tap was in a hidden organization) |\n\n## 6. External issues\n\nThe issue asks to report problems to other repositories when they are the cause. The candidate was\n[konard/links-visuals](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals), the blueprint the issue refers to. Its `grid.html` and\n`blueprint.html` already draw every link as a single SVG path with its own colour (`getLinkColor`). Root causes\n\n**Rain off the grid.** The old rain used 34 px columns while the CSS background grid has 64 px cells, and the grid\ndrifted on its own CSS animation (`grid-drift`, 24 s) independently of the canvas. Symbols and grid lines could never\nline up and slid apart over time. Now a column is 32 px (half a cell), columns start at x = 0 of the grid, and the\ndrift of the grid is set by the same animation loop that moves the canvas.\n\n**Hidden `S` and the overlapping arrow.** Words were placed at hand-picked offsets with an estimated width. Measuring\nthe old drawing ([`data/psd-old-overlaps.txt`](data/psd-old-overlaps.txt)) shows that \"Solution\" spanned x = 825.6–960\nwhile the final node spans 819–841, so the `S` was painted behind the node, and \"decomposition\" ended at x = 281.9\nwhile its arrow started at x = 280. The fix removes the guesswork: every label has a fixed `textLength`, so its width\ndoes not depend on the font that loaded, and nodes and arrows are computed from those widths. A test checks that no\nlabel touches another label, node or arrow.\n\n**Broken and one-sided links.** The symbols of issue #7 drew a link as separate pieces: a dot for the middle and two\nline segments to the ends. That made every link look split in the middle (img5–img7). A self-reference was a single\nloop on one side (\"eyeglasses\"). Links also all had the same colour. Now each link is one path: bar → own middle →\narrow, built from cubic Bézier segments whose tangents match where they meet. Each link has its own colour. A\nself-reference is a loop mirrored around the middle, so (1: 1 1) is ∞.\n\n**Missing networks.** The old set came from a generator that had no zero link and listed only a sample of networks.\nWith the zero link, N real links have 2N references, each one of N + 1 values. That gives (N + 1)^(2N) networks:\n4, 81, 4,096 and 390,625. Grouping networks that differ only by renaming links 1…N (0 stays fixed) leaves 4, 45, 720\nand 16,900 classes by Burnside's lemma. Brute force in [`data/count-networks.txt`](data/count-networks.txt) gives the\nsame numbers. The gallery shows every network page by page, because 390,625 symbols cannot be drawn at once.\n\n**Organizations, empty repositories and broken forks on the site.** The collection of issue #7 took every non-fork\npublic repository of the user and of every organization they had committed to. It had no notion of value for a\nvisitor. GitHub's `isFork` is false for a repository whose history was pushed rather than forked. That is what\nhappened with konard/slava: 49 of the 54 commits of konard/sbt, for example, are by another person. So such\nrepositories counted as original work. The fix collects health facts for every repository (size, files, root commit,\nupstream visibility) and hides them by explicit rules:\n\n| Reason | Repositories |\n| --- | --- |\n| hidden organization | 32 |\n| empty | 63 |\n| broken fork | 26 |\n| copy of a project that is not public | 86 |\n| deleted since the collection | 1 |\n\nThe full list, with names except for the non-public copies, is in\n[`data/repository-health-rules.txt`](data/repository-health-rules.txt). Only 3 copies of public projects remain,\nshown as forks. Their originals are MixaByk1996's elements-app, laravel-docker-project and gamestock.shop.\n\n**\"Client copies\" wording.** Repositories copied from other people were labelled \"copies of client projects kept for\nhistory\" and counted (89) on the Repositories page. That presented private work as a feature. Now only forks of\npublic projects are shown, and nothing about non-public originals is stored. The collector records just\n`{ \"public\": false }`, with no name.\n\n**Experience \"All\" showed few repositories.** Without a role, the page showed 6 examples per profession\n(`slice(0, 6)`). Now it shows every picked repository of every profession (13 professions, 114 repositories).\n\nThe site before and after:\n\n| | Before | After |\n| --- | --- | --- |\n| Original repositories | 525 in 15 organizations | 434 (146 personal, 288 in 8 organizations) |\n| Copies | 89 \"client copies\" | 3 forks of public projects |\n| Mirrors | 96 | 88 |\n| Stars | 993 | 982 |\n| Languages | 73 | 66 |\n| npm packages | 222 | 220 (Homebrew card gone: its only tap was in a hidden organization) |\n\n## 6. External issues\n\nThe issue asks to report problems to other repositories when they are the cause. The candidate was\n[konard/links-visuals](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals), the blueprint the issue refers to. Its `grid.html` and\n`blueprint.html` already draw every link as a single SVG path with its own colour (`getLinkColor`). The defects of\nimg5–img7 came from this site's own renderer (`src/links/glyph.js` of issue #7), not from links-visuals code. They are\nfixed here. links-visuals is an interactive editor and does not enumerate or encode networks, so the zero-link encoding\ndoes not apply to it. No other external project is involved, so no issue was filed.\n\n## 7. Debug tools\n\n| Tool | What it prints |\n| --- | --- |\n| `node experiments/collect-repository-health.cjs [out] --verbose` | Every repository with its root commit author and date, upstream visibility (`<- (not public)` without a name), retries and split batches when GitHub answers 502. |\n| `node experiments/repository-health-rules.cjs` | Every hidden repository grouped by reason; copies of non-public projects only as a count. |\n| `npm run build:data` | Totals and `not shown: 63 empty, 32 hidden organization, 26 broken fork, 86 original is not public, 1 deleted`. |\n| `node experiments/psd-old-overlaps.mjs` | Measured spans of the old diagram labels against nodes and arrows. |\n| `node experiments/count-networks.mjs` | Networks and classes of 1–4 links by brute force and by formula, with the first codes. |\n| `node experiments/contact-sheet.mjs` | A PNG sheet of all symbols of a size, to look at every network at once. |\n\n## 8. Online research and existing components\n\n| Source | Used for |\n| --- | --- |\n| [konard/links-visuals](https://github.com/konard/links-visuals) | The look of a link: a bar at the source, the middle, an arrow at the target, one colour per link, curves with continuous tangents (\"The Continuity of Splines\" by Freya Holmér, credited in its README). |\n| [konard/twittermatrix](https://github.com/konard/twittermatrix) | The digital rain mechanics: one symbol per column per step and a fading trail. |\n| [Burnside's lemma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Burnside%27s_lemma) | Counting networks up to renaming links (the \"one per class\" view of the gallery). |\n| [Cubic Bézier curves](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/SVG/Tutorial/Paths) | Smooth links drawn as SVG paths and as `Path2D` in the rain canvas. |\n| [SVG `textLength` / `lengthAdjust`](https://docs.w3cub.com/svg/reference/attribute/textlength) | Fixed label widths that do not depend on which font is loaded. |\n| [konard/problem-solving](https://github.com/konard/problem-solving) | The original idea and drawing of the universal problem solving algorithm. |\n| [link-assistant/hive-mind](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind), [link-assistant/formal-ai](https://github.com/link-assistant/formal-ai) | Implementations of the algorithm that the method notes link to. |\n| Musk's five-step engineering process, first step \"make your requirements less dumb\" ([CleanTechnica](https://cleantechnica.com/2021/08/16/elon-musk-reveals-his-5-step-engineering-protocol/), from the 2021 Everyday Astronaut Starbase interview) | The step that sends the solver back to the formulation of the task. |\n\nNo library was added. Drawing 390,625 different networks needs a geometry that is specific to doublet links. Generic\ngraph layout libraries (Cytoscape, d3-force, GoJS, considered in the links-visuals history) draw edges between nodes.\nThey cannot draw links that point to the middles of other links, and they cannot draw self-references that pass\nthrough their own middle.\n\n## 9. A network of N links is 2N digits in base N + 1, so there are\n  (N + 1)^(2N) networks: one link gives 00₂, 10₂, 01₂, 11₂; two links run 00₃ 00₃ … 22₃ 22₃ (81); three links give\n  4,096 and four links 390,625. Grouping by renaming links leaves 4 / 45 / 720 / 16,900 classes (Burnside), and a brute\n  force in `experiments/count-networks.mjs` gives the same counts.\n- **Drawing.** Each link is one continuous Bézier curve in its own colour: a bar at the source, then its own middle,\n  then an arrow at the target. Nothing breaks the line in the middle. Self-references are symmetric, so (1: 1 1) is a\n  figure eight (∞), also inside larger networks. Tests check that every network is drawable, that tangents are\n  continuous, that the figures are symmetric, and that ends touch the middles they refer to.\n- **Gallery.** \"Every configuration of 1–4 links\" is now on the Research page as well as Art. It shows the formula and\n  base subscripts, every network page by page, or one per class.\n- **Random network on click.** Clicking a network symbol shows a random network, with small labels for the math\n  notation and the links notation.\n- **Rain on the grid.** Exactly two symbol columns per 64 px grid cell, starting at the grid lines. The rain drives the\n  grid drift, so the two never slide apart.\n\n![gallery](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-9-5afd78997696/docs/case-studies/issue-9/screenshots/after-network-gallery.png?raw=true)\n![random network](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-9-5afd78997696/docs/case-studies/issue-9/screenshots/after-meta-theory-random-network.png?raw=true)\n![rain on the grid](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-9-5afd78997696/docs/case-studies/issue-9/screenshots/after-rain-on-grid-debug.png?raw=true)\n\n## Universal problem solving\n\n- **Layout.** Labels have fixed widths (`textLength`), and nodes and arrows are placed from those widths. #9\n\nEach item of the issue is listed below with its solution and the test that checks it. The full analysis is in the\ncase study [`docs/case-studies/issue-9/README.md`](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-9-5afd78997696/docs/case-studies/issue-9/README.md).\nIt covers the timeline, a requirement → solution → test table, root causes, research and debug tools.\n\n## Link networks\n\n- **Encoding with the zero link.** 0 is \"nothing\". A network of N links is 2N digits in base N + 1, so there are\n  (N + 1)^(2N) networks: one link gives 00₂, 10₂, 01₂, 11₂; two links run 00₃ 00₃ … 22₃ 22₃ (81); three links give\n  4,096 and four links 390,625. Grouping by renaming links leaves 4 / 45 / 720 / 16,900 classes (Burnside), and a brute\n  force in `experiments/count-networks.mjs` gives the same counts.\n- **Drawing.** Each link is one continuous Bézier curve in its own colour: a bar at the source, then its own middle,\n  then an arrow at the target. Nothing breaks the line in the middle. Self-references are symmetric, so (1: 1 1) is a\n  figure eight (∞), also inside larger networks. Tests check that every network is drawable, that tangents are\n  continuous, that the figures are symmetric, and that ends touch the middles they refer to.\n- **Gallery.** \"Every configuration of 1–4 links\" is now on the Research page as well as Art. It shows the formula and\n  base subscripts, every network page by page, or one per class.\n- **Random network on click.** Clicking a network symbol shows a random network, with small labels for the math\n  notation and the links notation.\n- **Rain on the grid.** Exactly two symbol columns per 64 px grid cell, starting at the grid lines. The rain drives the\n  grid drift, so the two never slide apart.\n\n![gallery](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-9-5afd78997696/docs/case-studies/issue-9/screenshots/after-network-gallery.png?raw=true)\n![random network](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-9-5afd78997696/docs/case-studies/issue-9/screenshots/after-meta-theory-random-network.png?raw=true)\n![rain on the grid](https://github.com/konard/konard.github.io/blob/issue-9-5afd78997696/docs/case-studies/issue-9/screenshots/after-rain-on-grid-debug.png?raw=true)\n\n## Universal problem solving\n\n- **Layout.** Labels have fixed widths (`textLength`), and nodes and arrows are placed from those widths. The \"S\" of\n  \"Solution\" was hidden behind the final node (825.6–960 against 819–841), and \"decomposition\" ran into its arrow\n  (281.9 > 280).
